title: Multi-Stream Perfusion Bioreactor Integrated with Outlet Fractionation for Dynamic Cell Culture
protocol: Prepare two lengths of silicone tubing (1.6 mm inner diameter) for each cell culture to be perfused.
Label both ends of each piece of tubing with unique identifiers using labeled tape.
Obtain a silicone stopper for each well of the well plate to fit snugly and form an airtight seal.
Trim excess material from the bottoms of the stoppers so they fit into the wells while leaving space inside.
Push two blunt 18 G needles through each stopper, one at the top as inlet and one at the bottom as outlet.
Adjust the heights of the needles within the plugged well to determine the stable liquid level during perfusion.
Clean and sterilize parts using 0.1 N NaOH followed by deionized water rinse if previously used.
Autoclave or otherwise ensure sterility of all parts.
Laser-cut the multi-head dispenser model from a computer-aided design program or provided DXF file.
Cut the design from a 1/8 in acrylic sheet using a laser cutter.
Remove the three screws attaching the dispensing head to the moving base of the fraction collector.
Align the three smallest holes in the multi-head dispenser with the screw holes in the moving base.
Screw the screws back through the aligned holes to attach the multi-head dispenser.
Adjust the tightness of the three screws to angle the multi-head dispenser up and down until the row of dispensing holes is aligned with the collection tubes below it.
Carefully place 300 μL pipette tips through the desired holes to serve as dispensing tips.
Set up pumps and syringes for tracer pulse as shown in Figure 2.
Choose a background solution to represent the medium that will be used during cell culture experiments.
Ensure the background solution has similar mass transfer properties to the medium.
Choose a tracer substance to represent the solute of interest during cell culture experiments.
Ensure the tracer has similar mass transfer properties to the solute and its concentration can be measured.
Dissolve the tracer substance in the background solution to make the tracer solution.
Fill one syringe with a background solution.
Load the syringe containing the background solution into one syringe pump.
Fill another syringe with tracer solution.
Load the syringe containing the tracer solution into the second syringe pump.
Connect both syringes to two of the three ports of a four-way stopcock using Luer connectors.
Close the stopcock to the background solution.
Pump the tracer solution into the stopcock until it begins to drip out the open port.
Stop the pump and do not adjust the syringe further.
Close the stopcock to the tracer solution.
Pump the background solution into the stopcock until all residual tracer solution has been flushed out of the open port.
Stop the pump and do not adjust the syringe further.
Set up the flow system component of interest.
Set up the fraction collector.
Ensure the component to be measured ends with a piece of downstream tubing of suitable length and flexibility to reach the fraction collector during operation.
Insert the end of the downstream tubing into a pipette tip dispenser in the multi-head dispenser such that it is snugly connected.
Attach the open port of the four-way stopcock to the inlet of the component to be measured.
Pump background solution through the component until it begins to drip out of the fraction collector dispensing tip.
Stop the pump.
Set the pump for the tracer solution to the desired flow rate.
Close the stopcock to the background solution and start the flow of the tracer solution.
Start the fraction collector simultaneously with the flow of tracer solution.
Continue the flow of tracer solution for 10 minutes at a flow rate of 1 mL/h.
Stop the tracer solution pump after the pulse period.
Quickly close the stopcock to the tracer solution.
Restart the flow of background solution at the same flow rate.
Allow the background solution to flow and fractions to be collected until all of the tracer has passed through the system and into the collected fractions.
Stop the system and measure the tracer concentration in the fractions.
Only include fractions that were dispensed completely.
Calculate the residence time distribution (RTD) from measured data in MATLAB.
Produce a .xlsx file containing the concentration data in the format of the example_tracer_data.xlsx spreadsheet provided.
Enter the concentration values of the tracer in the fractions in chronological order from left to right in row 2.
Enter the time elapsed from the start of the pulse to the end of the last fraction in cell A5.
Enter the length of the tracer pulse in minutes in cell A8.
Save the .xlsx file in the MATLAB directory.
Open the RTD_From_Data.m script, from Supplementary File 3, in the MATLAB editor.
Replace the name of the .xlsx file in the parentheses in the first line of the Load Data section with the name of the new .xlsx data file.
Run the script.
Ensure that the script successfully performs RTD analysis.
Produce a plot of the RTD.
Find the time vector (t) and associated RTD values vector (Et).
Open the Fit_RTD_Function.m script in the MATLAB editor from Supplementary File 4.
Choose one of the three commented-out model functions to fit to the RTD.
Remove the comments in the section containing the chosen model function.
Change initial guesses for the parameters appropriate for the RTD.
Run the script to produce a plot of the fit function overlaid on the RTD data.
Print the fit parameter values for the function.
If the fit is poor or errors occur, change parameter initial guesses and run again.
Choose either one signal and one RTD or two RTDs to convolve.
Open the Signal_Convolution.m script in the MATLAB editor.
Define one vector of evenly spaced time points for each signal in the desired units.
Create a corresponding vector of signal values at those times for each signal.
Ensure the vectors of the two signals have the same number of elements and size time steps.
Enter the two signals into MATLAB.
Run the script to obtain the time and signal vectors of the output signal.
Prepare the well plate culture with the appropriate medium depth for perfusion.
Perform any final medium changes, stimulations, or other desired steps prior to beginning perfusion.
Centrifuge suspension cells to ensure they are on the bottom of the well plate.
Insert stoppers with needles into the well plate cultures under sterile conditions.
Pull up the needles and lower them to the desired height for perfusion.
Cap the needles with male Luer caps.
Keep the whole well plate in an incubator until use.
Under sterile conditions, fill one syringe for each culture with enough medium plus additional volume to fill the upstream tubing.
Attach the upstream tubing to the syringe using a female-to-barb Luer connector.
Insert a male-to-barb Luer connector on the other end of the tube.
Dispense medium from the syringe until the upstream tube is entirely filled with medium.
Cap the open end of the upstream tube with a female Luer cap.
Under sterile conditions, insert a male-to-barb Luer connector into one end of the downstream tubing.
Cap the end of the downstream tube with a female Luer cap.
Bundle together the capped ends of all upstream and downstream tubes.
Push the bundled tubes from the outside to the inside through the incubator port.
Load the syringes into the syringe pump.
Insert the open ends of the downstream tubes into the dispensing pipette tips of the multi-head dispenser of the fraction collector.
Pull as much slack of the upstream tubes as possible into the incubator to maximize tubing length through which medium can receive heat and CO2 from the incubator air.

While holding these in place, pull the downstream tubes out of the incubator just enough so that they reach the furthest extended point on the fraction collector while keeping capped ends inside the incubator.
For each plugged well, quickly uncap the needles and upstream and downstream tubes for that well.
Attach them together with their Luer connectors.
Briefly run the syringe pump at a relatively high speed to ensure all streams are flowing properly.
Continue running the pump until all downstream tubes are filled with medium if desired; otherwise stop the pump.
Set the syringe pump flow rate and frequency of fraction collection.
Start both machines simultaneously to begin the experiment.
Collect fractions for the desired experiment duration.
Prepare two media for perfusion, labeling one as medium 1 and the other as medium 2.
Fill a first syringe with enough medium 1 to last throughout its dispensation plus additional volume to fill the perfusion system initially.
Fill a second syringe with sufficient medium 2 for its entire dispensation period.
Connect both syringes to two of the three ports on a four-way stopcock, ensuring any necessary tubing is in place.
Close the stopcock to medium 1 and dispense medium 2 into it until dripping occurs from an open port.
Close the stopcock to medium 2 and flush out residual medium 2 with medium 1 until no more drips occur.
Attach upstream tubing to the open stopcock port using a female-to-barb Luer connector, and insert a male-to-barb Luer connector at the other end of the tube.
Dispense medium 1 from its syringe until the entire upstream tube is filled with it.
Load both syringes into separate syringe pumps for dispensing.
Set the flow rate on the syringe pump for medium 1, and configure the frequency for fraction collection.
Start both machines simultaneously to initiate the experiment.
Quickly stop the syringe pump for medium 1 when changing the medium source.
Turn the stopcock closed to medium 1.
Start the syringe pump for medium 2.
Collect fractions for the desired experiment duration.
Set up the perfusion system with a stirred tank to mimic pharmacokinetics.
Obtain pharmacokinetic data for the drug of interest.
Ensure that the data consists of a concentration peak followed by an exponential decay.
Set the peak to time 0 and remove data points prior to the peak.
Use Stirred_Tank_Fit.m script to fit the stirred tank RTD equation to the data.
Input v (the desired perfusion flow rate) and the data as vectors into the script, along with t and C for time values and concentration values respectively.
Run the script to print parameter V, which is the required stirred tank volume.
Plan a layout for the perfusion system including two syringe pumps and a plate shaker upstream of the incubator.
Measure RTDs of the perfusion system components beyond the stopcock.
Perform signal convolution of the RTDs with various drug pulse durations and concentrations to find an appropriate pharmacokinetic profile.
Use an additional well plate as the stirred tank for each perfused culture.
Fill each well with the required volume of medium, V.
Plug the wells with initially pulled-up needles pushed to the bottom, then cap the needles.
Load syringes into the syringe pumps.
Quickly connect tubing from the syringes to the capped inlet needles of the stirred tanks.
Connect cell culture upstream tube inlets to the outlet needles of the stirred tanks.
Switch to dispensing medium 2 containing the drug at the desired time.
Switch back to medium 1 when the drug infusion is complete.
